newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunfire erupts at Islamist protest in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Gunfire erupts at Islamist protest in Pakistan.

text.p: Two policemen and the driver of a local government official were wounded on Sunday in a clash between police and Islamist protesters in a town in Pakistan's Punjab province, state-run radio reported.

It said gunfire erupted near the town of Saray Alamgir, about 100 km (62 miles) southeast of Islamabad, after police intercepted Jamaat-i-Islami party vehicles heading for the capital to join a planned sit-in outside parliament.
The radio said one of the wounded was the driver of the assistant commissioner of Jehlum district in Punjab province. It did not say how seriously any of the three had been hurt.
The shooting occurred at about 7.30 a.m. (0230 GMT) after police teargassed the Jamaat-i-Islami procession.
The cavalcade drove on, only to be intercepted about half an hour later further down the road. The protesters burst through the second barricade, pelting stones at police.

The security forces have taken elaborate precautions to prevent the Islamic militants from carrying out plans to hold a sit-in outside parliament in Islamabad to protest at alleged corruption under Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government.
